title: How to Patch a Small Hole in Drywall
metaDescription: Nail hole, doorknob dent, or small drywall hole (under 2 inches)? Here's how to patch it invisibly with spackle in under an hour, no mesh patch needed.
symptom: A small hole or dent in the wall (roughly nail-hole to golf-ball size) from a doorknob, picture hook, or minor impact.
partsNeeded: Lightweight spackle or vinyl spackling compound

steps.heading: Clean up the hole edges
steps.body: Remove any loose or crumbling drywall paper/debris around the hole with your fingers or the putty knife edge so the spackle has a clean surface to bond to.

steps.heading: Apply the first layer of spackle
steps.body: Load a small amount onto the putty knife and press it into the hole, then draw the knife across at a slight angle to fill it flush with the surrounding wall. Don't worry about it being perfectly smooth yet.

steps.heading: Let it dry fully
steps.body: Lightweight spackle typically dries in 30-60 minutes, but check the product label — it should feel fully hard and slightly lighter/whiter in color when cured, not tacky.

steps.heading: Sand it smooth
steps.body: Using a fine sanding sponge, sand in small circles until the patch is flush with the wall. Wipe away dust with a slightly damp cloth.

steps.heading: Apply a thin second coat if needed
steps.body: Spackle shrinks slightly as it dries, so a small dip is common after the first coat. A thin second coat, dried and sanded the same way, usually gets it fully flush.

steps.heading: Prime and paint to match
steps.body: Spackled areas absorb paint differently than the surrounding wall, so a quick coat of primer (or a paint-and-primer touch-up product) before your matching paint color prevents a visible flat spot once painted.

whenToCallAPro: This size of hole is genuinely beginner-friendly — a professional isn't typically needed. If you're dealing with a hole larger than a couple inches, or several holes close together weakening a section of wall, see the guide for larger drywall holes instead.
safetyWarnings: Wear a dust mask when sanding dried spackle, especially in an enclosed room.
